# {{project.name}}

> Scoped internationalization through formatter functions and native Custom Elements built on `@beforesemicolon/web-component`.

Package: `{{project.name}}`
Version: `{{project.version}}`
Documentation: https://intl.beforesemicolon.com/documentation/
Complete context: https://intl.beforesemicolon.com/llms-full.txt

Use this file as the authoritative compact contract when generating Intl code. Use the exact `intl*` API names documented here; do not substitute framework i18n hooks, context providers, or undocumented `format*` aliases.

## Before Semicolon ecosystem

The packages form one composable browser ecosystem:

1. `@beforesemicolon/markup` owns reactive rendering, state, effects, refs, and helpers.
2. `@beforesemicolon/web-component` owns reactive native Custom Elements and re-exports Markup.
3. `@beforesemicolon/router` owns navigation and route-aware rendering.
4. `@beforesemicolon/intl` owns locale scopes, message loading, translations, fallback behavior, and internationalized formatting.

Intl depends on Web Component for its elements, but it exports Intl components, runtime APIs, and formatter APIs—not `html`, `WebComponent`, or Router APIs. Import those capabilities from their owning packages.

Canonical ecosystem contracts:

- https://markup.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt
- https://web-component.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt
- https://router.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt

## Installation and setup

```bash
npm install @beforesemicolon/intl
```

The package entrypoint registers all Intl Custom Elements and exports the runtime and formatter APIs:

```javascript
import {
    initIntl,
    setLocale,
    intlMsg,
    intlNumber,
    intlDateTime,
} from '@beforesemicolon/intl'
```

For direct browser use, load Web Component first:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@beforesemicolon/web-component/dist/client.js"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@beforesemicolon/intl/dist/client.js"></script>
<script>
    const { initIntl, setLocale, intlMsg, intlNumber } = BFS.INTL
</script>
```

## Core mental model

- An Intl runtime stores the active locale, direction, fallback locale, messages, loading status, and formatter caches.
- `<intl-locale>` provides a runtime scope to descendant Intl components.
- Nested locale providers inherit parent and fallback messages unless overridden.
- Formatter functions work without DOM components and may target a specific runtime scope.
- Visible fallback text in Intl elements remains useful before messages load and when a key is missing.

## Component-first usage

```html
<intl-locale
    locale="en-US"
    fallback-locale="en"
    src-dir="/locales"
    update-document
>
    <h1><intl-msg key="checkout.title">Checkout</intl-msg></h1>
    <intl-number type="currency" currency="USD">1299.99</intl-number>
    <intl-datetime date-style="medium" time-zone="UTC">
        2026-01-01T10:00:00Z
    </intl-datetime>
</intl-locale>
```

Use one top-level provider for the main application locale. Use nested providers only for intentional localized subtrees.

Primary components:

- `<intl-locale>`: runtime provider and locale message loader.
- `<intl-msg>`: message lookup and value interpolation.
- `<intl-number>`: number, currency, percent, and unit formatting.
- `<intl-datetime>`: date and time formatting.
- `<intl-duration>`: duration formatting.
- `<intl-rel-time>`: relative time formatting, optionally live.
- `<intl-list>`: conjunction, disjunction, and unit lists.
- `<intl-name>`: language, region, currency, and other display names.
- `<intl-plural>`: plural category selection.

## Runtime API

Create an isolated scope when localization should not use the default singleton:

```javascript
import { createIntl, getIntl, loadLocale, setLocale } from '@beforesemicolon/intl'

const checkoutIntl = createIntl({
    locale: 'en-US',
    fallbackLocale: 'en',
    messages: {
        checkout: {
            total: 'Total: {amount}',
        },
    },
})

getIntl(checkoutIntl)
await loadLocale('pt-CV', checkoutIntl)
await setLocale('pt-CV', checkoutIntl)
```

Runtime APIs:

- `createIntl(options)` creates an independent runtime.
- `initIntl(options)` initializes or replaces the default runtime configuration.
- `getIntl(scope?)` returns the provided runtime or the default runtime.
- `loadLocale(locale?, scope?)` loads messages for a locale.
- `setLocale(locale, scope?)` activates and loads a locale.
- `subscribeIntl(listener, scope?)` observes runtime snapshots and returns an unsubscribe function.
- `destroyIntl(scope?)` disposes a runtime.
- `resetIntl()` resets the default runtime.
- `getLocaleDirection(locale)` returns `ltr` or `rtl`.

## Formatter API

Use these exact exported names:

```javascript
import {
    intlMsg,
    intlNumber,
    intlDateTime,
    intlDuration,
    intlRelTime,
    intlList,
    intlName,
    intlPlural,
} from '@beforesemicolon/intl'

intlMsg('checkout.total', { amount: '$12.00' }, { scope: checkoutIntl })
intlNumber(1200, { locale: 'en-US', style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' })
intlDateTime('2026-01-01T10:00:00Z', {
    locale: 'en-US',
    dateStyle: 'medium',
    timeZone: 'UTC',
})
intlDuration(3600000, { fields: 'hours', style: 'short' })
intlRelTime(Date.now() + 60000, { unit: 'auto' })
intlList(['A', 'B', 'C'], { type: 'conjunction' })
intlName('PT', { type: 'region' })
intlPlural(2, { one: 'item', other: 'items' })
```

Read the formatter-specific pages for supported option names. Do not translate native `Intl` option names into framework conventions.

## Message files and fallback

Message files are JSON objects. Nested keys use dot notation:

```json
{
    "checkout": {
        "title": "Checkout",
        "total": "Total: {amount}"
    }
}
```

```html
<intl-msg key="checkout.total" values='{"amount":"$12.00"}'>
    Total
</intl-msg>
```

- `src-dir="/locales"` loads `/locales/{locale}.json`.
- Use `src` when a scope owns an exact bundle URL.
- Keep fallback text readable for loading, missing keys, crawlers, and no-JavaScript output.
- Put `update-document` only on the top-most application scope so document language and direction have one owner.

## Locale changes

```javascript
import { setLocale } from '@beforesemicolon/intl'

const selector = document.querySelector('#locale')
selector?.addEventListener('change', async (event) => {
    const locale = event.target.value
    await setLocale(locale)
})
```

Subscribed components update from the active runtime without a page reload.

## Router and Web Component composition

Intl components may appear inside Router routes and custom application components:

```bash
npm install @beforesemicolon/router @beforesemicolon/intl
```

```javascript
import '@beforesemicolon/router'
import '@beforesemicolon/intl'
import { WebComponent, html } from '@beforesemicolon/web-component'
```

```html
<page-route path="/invoices/:invoiceId">
    <intl-locale locale="en-US" src="/locales/en-US.invoice.json">
        <h1><intl-msg key="invoice.title">Invoice</intl-msg></h1>
        <intl-number type="currency" currency="USD">250</intl-number>
    </intl-locale>
</page-route>
```

Router changes URLs and route content. Intl changes locale output. Web Component owns reusable application elements, and Markup owns their reactive templates.

For CDN use, load scripts in this order: Web Component, then Router and/or Intl.

## Rules for generated code

- Use the exported `intlMsg`, `intlNumber`, `intlDateTime`, `intlDuration`, `intlRelTime`, `intlList`, `intlName`, and `intlPlural` names.
- Use Intl components for visible localized DOM and formatter functions for values needed in JavaScript.
- Keep message keys semantic and nested by feature rather than duplicating visible English text as keys.
- Provide readable fallback content in HTML.
- Keep one owner for document language and direction.
- Import `html` and `WebComponent` from Web Component and navigation APIs from Router.
- Do not invent React context, hooks, directives, or translation syntax.
